title: Revolutionary FAR Overhaul — What It Is
summary: The RFO, effective April 2025, is the most comprehensive revision to the Federal Acquisition Regulation since 1984. It restructures the FAR to reduce regulatory burden, accelerate acquisitions, and align with commercial best practices.
legacyText: TODO: paste overview legacy context text here
rfoText: TODO: paste RFO overview text here

legacy.t: The FAR was characterized as 'an excessive and overcomplicated regulatory framework' requiring wholesale reform.
Prior revision cycles were incremental; the last structural overhaul dates to the original 1984 FAR publication.

rfo.t: Issued April 15, 2025; stated goal is the 'most agile, effective, and efficient procurement system in the world.'
Consolidates, reorders, and simplifies dozens of parts; many subparts renumbered or merged.

title: FAR 1.102 — Statement of Guiding Principles
summary: Guiding principles updated in the RFO to elevate commercial best practices and innovation alongside traditional government acquisition values.
legacyText: TODO: paste legacy FAR 1.102 text here

legacy.t: Guiding principles focused on competition, best value, and maintaining the public trust.

rfo.t: Updated goals add 'speed' and 'commercial alignment' alongside the legacy four objectives.
New language encourages agencies to treat commercial best practices as the baseline, not the exception.

title: FAR 2.101 — Commercial Product / Commercial Service
summary: The single 'commercial item' definition is split into 'commercial product' and 'commercial service' throughout the RFO — the single largest terminology change affecting dozens of clauses.
legacyText: TODO: paste legacy FAR 2.101 commercial item definition here
rfoText: TODO: paste RFO FAR 2.101 commercial product/service definitions here

legacy.t: 'Commercial item' defined as one broad category encompassing both products and services sold in the commercial marketplace.

rfo.t: 'Commercial item' retired; replaced by 'commercial product' and 'commercial service' as two separate defined terms with distinct criteria.
The split clarifies different legal treatments: commercial services are assessed on labor and performance standards, products on marketplace availability.

title: FAR 2.101 — Acquisition Thresholds

legacy.t: Micro-purchase threshold: $10,000 (general); $2,000 for construction subject to Davis-Bacon.

rfo.t: Threshold amounts retained; applicability notes updated to reflect Part 6 reorganization.
New definition consolidates all threshold references that were scattered across multiple parts.

title: FAR 6.001 — Applicability

rfo.t: Added '(but see 13.501)' in paragraph (a) to close the loop on commercial sole-source competition policy.

legacyText: TODO: paste legacy DFARS 225.7002 text here
rfoText: TODO: paste revised DFARS 225.7002 text here

legacy.t: Specialty metals (titanium, steel alloys, tungsten) used in DoD weapons systems must be melted or produced in the U.S. or qualifying countries; exceptions for commercial items and de minimis.

rfo.t: Qualifying country list and de minimis exception thresholds reviewed; electronic recordkeeping of specialty metal origin updated.
